Definition: from G1487 and G4007; if perhaps:--if so be (that), seeing, though.
BiblicalUsage: This phrase means if indeed or if so be, and in the Greek text it is written as a single word, with if and indeed joined together. Paul says you are in the Spirit if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you, and that we are heirs of God if so be we suffer with Him. The phrase does not doubt; it states the condition on which the promise stands.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe if so be is a promise with a condition attached, and the condition is real, because the Spirit's presence is the proof of the promise.
